item.title: How China’s ‘carrier nannies’ are powering the Liaoning’s long Pacific push
item.description: Chinese replenishment ships were seen repeatedly transiting two major waterways around Japan as the Liaoning aircraft carrier conducted an extended western Pacific Ocean deployment that could test its 40-day endurance record. According to Japanese defence ministry statements, the ships made at least eight crossings through the Miyako Strait and the Osumi Strait between October 16 and Wednesday, the South China Morning Post calculated. item.title: China’s first lady Peng Liyuan again lets her English do the talking in welcoming Trump
item.description: Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan again let her English do the talking as she accompanied President Xi Jinping in welcoming his US counterpart Donald Trump and other leaders to Shenzhen for the Apec summit’s welcome dinner. item.title: Asean, Canada speed up trade pact over Trump, but can it curb US reliance?
item.description: Canada and Asean are closing in on a free-trade agreement after five years of negotiations – a potential breakthrough that could deepen their economic ties and give businesses more opportunities amid growing uncertainty over global trade. Its greatest value, though, might come from strengthening supply chains rather than reshaping trade, according to analysts. item.title: Xi greets Takaichi with a smile – but no words – as China-Japan freeze lingers
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping had their first in-person interaction in Shenzhen since last autumn, when ties froze due to her controversial remarks on Taiwan. Takaichi shook hands with Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, as they posed for greeting photos ahead of the customary Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) “family photo” on Wednesday evening, according to a live feed of a welcome dinner for the Apec gathering. item.title: Spanish court opens sexual abuse probe into Julio Iglesias
item.description: A Spanish court opened a probe into veteran crooner Julio Iglesias on Wednesday after two women ex-employees filed a complaint against him for alleged sexual abuse, which he denies. The announcement marks a turnaround after a first complaint was shelved on the grounds that Spain had no jurisdiction to try crimes committed in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic.
